Kai: Quick update — ran a focused microbenchmark for fused-epilogue + QKV-packed kernels against paged-KV workloads. Seeing a weird L2 thrash spike when epilogue prefetch is enabled + page faults on 4K KV slices.
Alex: Can you paste the perf output?
Kai: Pasting the run (short):
```
./bench --model gpt-medium --bs 1,8,32 --seq 64,512 \
  --kernels fused_qkv_epilogue --kv-mode paged --prefetch on

Results:
  bs=1 seq=64   : 1200 tokens/s (stable)
  bs=8 seq=64   : 4300 tokens/s
  bs=1 seq=512  : 320 tokens/s (heavy variance)
  bs=8 seq=512  : 870 tokens/s -> large tail latency spikes

perf report: L2-load-misses +10x vs non-prefetch variant, STLB shootdowns reported
```
Maria: Huh. That suggests the prefetch touches many small KV pages and pollutes L2/TLB. Paged-KV is more sensitive because QKV packing expands working set per token.
Ben: Did you try prefetching only the epilogue buffers (out_q/out_kv) and not the packed QKV tile? Smaller prefetch stride maybe?
Kai: Yes — tried `prefetch=epilogue_only` and `stride=64` — reduced L2 misses ~3x, but throughput still below non-fused baseline for bs=1 seq=512. Suspect memory-bandwidth + serialized cache lines from epilogue writebacks.
Alex: Could also be that our epilogue fusion serializes stores across lanes — if lanes hit different KV pages, we'll get terrible write-combine behavior. Any assembly / sasm trace?
Kai: Grabbed a perf trace. Key snippet:
```
mov.async bulk -> thread0
ld.global.ca [kv_page0] -> vreg
st.global.wb [out_q] -> vreg
ld.global.ca [kv_page128] -> vreg
```
Interleaving shows cross-page accesses in tight loop.
Maria: Two quick mitigations: (1) Lane-aware scheduling: keep contiguous lanes on same page when possible. (2) Epilogue staging buffer in L1-friendly tile and do an aggregated store to reduce writeback noise.
Ben: For (1) we could modify the batcher to coalesce requests by KV page id before issuing to kernel. But that changes latency SLOs for tail requests. Tradeoff.
Alex: Also, fallback policy: if paged-KV with seq>256 and bs<=2, disable epilogue prefetch or switch to non-packed QKV epilogue. Keep a small heuristic table in kernel chooser.
perf-bot: baseline comparison (non-fused qkv, no prefetch): bs=1 seq=512 -> 480 tokens/s; fused+prefetch -> 320 tokens/s; fused+epilogue_only -> 420 tokens/s.
Kai: Nice, perf-bot — that shows epilogue-only prefetch is the sweet-spot. Next step: patch kernel-chooser with a quick heuristic and run a 24h soak on the paged-KV multi-tenant cluster. I'll prototype lane-coalescing in the batcher as an opt-in flag.
Maria: If you prototype lane-coalescing, add a metric for 'page-hotness' per request so we can decide dynamically. Also add a canary that routes small-Seq VIP requests to non-coalesced path for safety.
Ben: FYI, I hit a similar L2/TLB issue last quarter with rotary-bias fusion; the mini-stage then store trick worked well. Will send the snippet.
Kai: Thanks — I'll take Ben's snippet + Maria's metric proposal. Ping me if you want to pair on the patch. :+1:
Alex: SG. Once we have the heuristic, we can wire it into rollout: start with 0.1 traffic, track p50/p95/p99 and CPU/GPU mem-bandwidth counters.
Kai: Plan set. I'll open an RFC draft in #eng-runtime and link the perf logs. Closing the loop here for now.
